tracks.narration: Thévenin gave us a voltage source. What if we want a current source instead?
Short the terminals together. The current that flows through that wire is I Norton — the short-circuit current of the network.
A Thévenin form on the left morphs into a Norton form on the right. The resistance is the same; the source flips from V Thevenin over R Thevenin volts to V Thevenin over R Thevenin amps in parallel.
Reconnect a load. The current source splits between R Norton and the load by the current-divider rule — and you get exactly the same I L as Thevenin predicted.
Pick whichever form makes the algebra easier — same load current either way.
